errors.text: The proposed mechanism asserts intrinsic entropy stabilization and sluggish diffusion, whereas the target behavior is active, non-sluggish diffusion controlled by surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation.

The material is not reconstructed: the target is equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt in sub-10 nm FCC multi-twinned or icosahedral particles, while the hypothesis gives an unspecified and internally inconsistent '50:20:20:20:20' composition and particles below 50 nm.
The intervention and conditions are fundamentally different: prolonged 800–1200 °C argon annealing replaces in situ vacuum heating from 298 to 973 K at 1 K/s.

The predicted retention of a single phase, grain size, and hardness misses the observed surface segregation, reshaping, loss of 2–4 nm particles, Au/Cu evaporation, and approximately 22% size reduction.
The cited evidence primarily concerns bulk or micrometer-scale HEAs and does not establish sluggish diffusion or entropy stabilization in sub-10 nm nanoparticles where surface diffusion dominates.
The proposed diffusion measurement from EDS line scans and Vickers hardness testing is poorly suited to isolated sub-50 nm nanoparticles.
